Slice 3 (kit, Q4) — A/B on “Published guide”

Project Raw Footage Test, shot published-guide (cutaway, anchored 57–65s, asset site = full capture of the learnwithhasan.com guide page). Same brief for every version; provider claude-subscription (claude-opus-5); every regen was a single pass with 0 fix attempts.

Verdict: the kit moves screencast-shaped shots — but only once the whole pipeline cooperates. The manifest alone changed nothing (v2); prompt hardening alone changed nothing (v3, v4); the flip came when the verify step stopped rewriting contract-compliant code (SQ17) — v5 imports @vidtsx/kit, renders the REAL captured page inside real browser chrome with a scripted scroll, pinned the kit snapshot into the project, and previews through the virtual module in the live Player.

The ladder (what each rung proves)

  • v1 (2026-08-19 baseline, flip the version picker to see it): hand-drawn mini-window, placeholder bars as “text”, three fake stat boxes; the provided screenshot asset was never used.
  • v2 — KIT manifest in the prompt: no kit import. Craft improved (real headline text, refined pills) = Layer A working, but chrome still hand-drawn. Also exposed: the verify step rewrote durationInFrames to durationInSeconds.
  • v3 — + “a brief that describes chrome is asking for the kit component” + kit exemplar: still no import — the model DEFINED its own const BrowserWindow.
  • v4 — + MUST / SUPERSEDES / “re-implementing a kit component is a defect”: still hand-rolled.
  • v5 — + SQ17 (verify reviews under the caller contract): import { BrowserWindow, CLAMP, EASINGS } from '@vidtsx/kit', real still as the page, nav script with scroll steps, project pin at kit/1.0.0/. v4→v5 isolates the verify step as the blocker.

v2 — kit live but unused (hand-drawn chrome, fake page)

v5 — kit used (real capture inside BrowserWindow, scripted scroll)
